title: Add behavior-evidence default with protection-test rule and examples
summary: Redo rejected job 20261015-095214-y8kr from the base (its edits were discarded): add a new defaults.toml entry requiring acceptance criteria to check the requested behavior, with protection/denial tests shown unprotected-as-root then refused and failing rather than skipping. Add worked examples and a test. Keep the diff minimal: no reader.md rewording and every CHANGELOG claim true. Audience: the reader, producer and verifier receiving rendered defaults.

defaults_applied.how: A unit test in defaults.rs asserts the new entry and its rendered first-sentence line; cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
The rule goes into the shared defaults every role receives, not into one prompt, and the earlier failure's cause (collateral edits and untrue changelog claims) is avoided by keeping the diff minimal.
One focused change: defaults entry, test, example doc and one changelog line.
Criteria require running cargo test and checking the diff for collateral changes.
Entry and examples are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The earlier changes were discarded, so the retry rebuilds the whole feature, not just the two repairs.
The defaults.toml entry is the only prompt-facing change; reader.md is left byte-identical unless the reader token budget in athena-context forces a change.
If reader.md must change, only the intended lines change, each instruction stays its own bullet, and the CHANGELOG says why.
The 'applies_to' of the new entry is ["*"] and its first sentence carries the core rule, since the rendered brief shows only the first sentence.

acceptance_criteria.text: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] entry (e.g. id "behavior-evidence") with applies_to ["*"], a source citing this request, and a statement whose FIRST sentence says criteria must check the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist.

The statement's later sentences require that a protection or denial test first shows the action succeeds without the protection, as the same user and environment the real component runs as (root), then shows it is refused, and that it fails, not skips or passes silently, if the environment cannot enforce the protection.

A new unit test in crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs parses the repository defaults.toml and asserts the new entry exists and its render() line contains the core rule. Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: it passes along with root_cause_default_leads_with_the_core_rule.

docs/design/defaults-loop.md has a worked example for a 'make X read-only' request whose criteria are: a write to X as root succeeds before protection; the same root write is refused after; the test fails, not skips, if the environment cannot enforce it (a root-bypassed file mode is not proof).

The same doc has a worked example for 'role calls a model' whose criteria run the role end to end and check the model request is observed (e.g. through the fake client) and its output is used, not merely that a client or config is wired in.

Outcome check for the reader: the rendered reader brief for the defaults set includes the new default line with the core rule, so a reader writing criteria for a read-only request sees it. Check by running the athena-context tests, which must still pass within the reader token budget.

`git diff` shows no collateral edits: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md is unchanged, or, if changed, differs only by the intended lines with every instruction still its own bullet. Each CHANGELOG.md claim under Unreleased / Added names only things present in the diff, with no claim about the reader prompt unless reader.md contains it.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass from the repository root.

out_of_scope: Building a pre-verification diff or changelog checker (the introspection's proposed code-check).
Changing how prompts are built beyond the defaults rendering.
Editing records/ or the owner's files.
departures: Slightly lower pass probability than the reference: the earlier attempt failed on the token budget for the rendered reader set, a risk that may recur.
